resources.summary: Community mod browse/discovery page for Elden Ring. It is a hosting/discovery page, not a loader or installer; per-mod target versions and requirements are user-published.

resources.name: Melty (PC mod and mashup platform)
resources.summary: Platform for discovering, publishing, and sharing user-made PC game mods and cross-game mashups, including creator workflows using coding agents or connected GitHub repositories. The website is a distribution/discovery service; its separate Windows desktop client is catalogued independently. It is not a universal runtime loader or compatibility certification.

resources.name: Melty Discover (user-published mods and mashups)
resources.summary: Melty's browse page for user-published mashups and mods. Listings have their own game, build, store, runtime, and dependency requirements; presence in the directory is not a compatibility statement for any other tool or game release.

resources.name: Melty Desktop App (Windows setup and launcher)
resources.summary: Windows-only client for one-click setup and launching of Melty mashups. Its Terms say it can inspect installed game versions, download mashup files and required tools, write into game folders after copying replaced files, locate and copy needed files from the user's own game installation locally, build components, and start games/programs/setup steps. It orchestrates per-mashup tooling; it is not a general-purpose runtime or a cross-game compatibility guarantee.

resources.name: Melty Terms of Service
resources.summary: Melty’s Terms, last updated 2026-10-06. They state every mod/mashup release is audited before publication by reading all release files (and source code when published from GitHub), require a successful run on its creator’s PC, and repeat the audit for each update; this is the provider’s description. The Terms state the creator-PC audit process; they do not provide a per-PC compatibility matrix for every mashup.

resources.name: Melty Privacy Policy
resources.summary: Melty Privacy Policy page, last updated 2026-10-06.

resources.name: PS5 RetroArch
resources.summary: Native RetroArch homebrew application for PlayStation 5, requiring an already configured compatible jailbreak/homebrew environment. Upstream’s inspected latest pre-release is v0.6.7-alpha.6 (2026-10-05); its README lists fifteen release cores and a local WebUI, while compatibility varies by core and workload. The project says it includes no games, BIOS, firmware, or decryption keys. This is a multi-system emulation frontend on PS5, not a PS5 game-modding tool.

resources.name: Factorio Lua API Documentation
resources.summary: Official reference for writing Factorio mods; the inspected docs identify version 2.1.21 and describe settings, prototype, and runtime stages with a modified Lua 5.2 API. This is a game-integrated mod API, not a universal loader; match mods and documentation to the installed Factorio version.

resources.name: Factorio Mod Portal
resources.summary: Official Factorio mod hosting and discovery portal linked from the game and API docs. The in-game manager downloads, updates, and enables mods; portal entries expose version-specific packages and history. Factorio-specific distribution, not a general mod API or compatibility guarantee.

resources.name: The Sims 4 Policy on Mods (EA Help)
resources.summary: EA's current Sims 4 mod policy page covers community-mod publication and platform guidance. This is policy documentation, not a public modding SDK or compatibility matrix.

resources.name: The Sims 4 Mods, Game Updates, and Error Codes (EA Help)
resources.summary: EA's official troubleshooting guide says game updates disable mods because EA does not screen or support them; mod compatibility varies by creator and patch, and outdated mods may need replacement. It is a version-status reference, not a loader or API.

resources.name: How to Install Mods in The Sims 4 (EA Help)
resources.summary: EA's official guide describes community-made Custom Content and Game Mods and states that mods are available on PC and Mac, not PlayStation or Xbox. This documents a title-specific player route and platform boundary; it is not an official mod SDK and does not validate individual mods or builds.

resources.name: Dwarf Fortress Modding Guide (Bay 12 Games)
resources.summary: Official Bay 12 guide for Dwarf Fortress 50.01 and later: native mods add objects/tiles through info.txt plus objects/graphics files, are selected when creating a world, and can be distributed through Steam Workshop or installed as folders/ZIPs. This is a built-in data-mod workflow, not a general plugin/runtime API or cross-version compatibility matrix.

resources.name: Call of Duty: Black Ops III Update 15.1 / Mod Tools Open Beta (official Steam)
resources.category: Game-specific modding SDKs and development APIs
resources.summary: Treyarch’s official Steam announcement documents the Black Ops III Mod Tools Open Beta for full-game Steam owners, including Radiant, APE, a Mod Tools Launcher, optional assets, and Steam Workshop. This is a title/store-specific authoring path, explicitly beta in the announcement; it does not establish compatibility for other Call of Duty titles, stores, or current builds.

resources.name: CRYENGINE Licensing and Crysis Mod SDK Scope (Crytek)
resources.summary: Crytek's official page says the original Crysis ModSDK is delivered with the game and that a Crysis Remastered Mod SDK is not currently planned. CRYENGINE developer tools are separate from retail-game mod kits; Crysis 2/3 SDK availability is not established.

resources.name: mod.io Console Platform Support Documentation
resources.summary: mod.io's provider documentation describes UGC integration support for Xbox One/Series, PlayStation 4/5, Nintendo Switch, and Switch 2. Console support is implemented through title-specific integrations; the documentation does not describe a player-side console mod tool or establish support for every title.

resources.name: The Witcher 3 Cross-Platform Mod Support (CD Projekt Red)
resources.summary: CD Projekt Red's official support guide (checked 2026-10-06) describes a title-specific in-game mod.io workflow on PC, PlayStation 5, Xbox Series X|S, and Nintendo Switch 2. Console availability is limited to mods tagged for console support; console modded saves disable trophies/achievements. This is an integrated path for The Witcher 3 only, not a general console modding API or guarantee for every mod.

resources.name: PS5SX2 (PCSX2 for PS5)
resources.summary: Native PlayStation 5 homebrew port of the PCSX2 PlayStation 2 emulator. The latest inspected release is PS5SX2 1.9 / build vk-285-130 (2026-10-05); upstream describes it as a passion project with rough edges, so per-game compatibility and performance remain unverified beyond its stated tests. Requires an already configured compatible homebrew environment.

resources.name: ProsperoEden (Eden for PS5)
resources.summary: Unofficial Eden Nintendo Switch emulator port for PS5 homebrew. The latest inspected release is v1.000.070 (2026-10-04), marked pre-release; upstream calls the project early alpha and says compatibility/performance vary by game, with video, audio, controls, and saves confirmed. Requires an existing compatible homebrew environment;.

resources.name: XPSemu (original Xbox for PS5)
resources.summary: Native PS5 port of xemu, the original Xbox emulator. The inspected Alpha 1 release (2026-10-01) is an early playable build with only a small, developer-reported game test set; it does not establish full-library compatibility. The project says games and system files are not bundled. Requires an already configured compatible homebrew environment

resources.name: PS5X360 (Xenia Canary for PS5)
resources.summary: Native PS5 port of Xenia Canary for Xbox 360 emulation. Upstream's inspected v0.5.6 release (2026-10-06) says compatibility is still developing and varies by game, firmware, and homebrew setup; it makes no full-library or fixed-frame-rate promise. It is an emulator port, not an Xbox 360 modding tool.

resources.name: PS5CEMU-HAR (Cemu and Azahar for PS5)
resources.summary: PS5 homebrew frontend pairing Cemu for Wii U emulation with Azahar for Nintendo 3DS emulation. The inspected v3.0.0 release (2026-10-04) reports that most Wii U titles tried so far are playable, while 3DS support is newer and less tested on real hardware. These are emulator ports, not Wii U/3DS-console modding paths

resources.name: Snes9x PS5
resources.summary: Native PS5 home-screen port of Snes9x for Super Nintendo emulation. The inspected v2.0 release (2026-10-03) identifies Snes9x 1.63; the repository says no games or BIOS are included. Compatibility remains title-specific. This is an emulator port, not SNES-console modding

resources.name: Porpoise (Dolphin for PS5)
resources.summary: Native PS5 homebrew frontend for the Dolphin GameCube/Wii emulator. The inspected releases page lists v2.1.1 (2026-10-06); PS5 development is early-stage, the main branch has newer unreleased commits, and the README appeared behind the release. Compatibility varies by title. The package lists no games, BIOS, or firmware; this is emulation, not GameCube/Wii-console modding.

resources.name: JADX (Android DEX/APK decompiler)
resources.summary: Command-line and GUI decompiler for Android DEX/APK inputs, with support for AAB/AAR and resource decoding. It reconstructs Java-like views rather than original Java/Kotlin source; output may be incomplete, especially for obfuscated or complex code. Latest inspected release: v1.5.6 (2026-07-10).

resources.name: Apktool (Android APK analysis)
resources.summary: Open-source Android APK reverse-engineering tool for inspecting decoded resources/manifest and DEX disassembly in Smali; the project also supports rebuilding packages. Latest inspected release: v3.0.3 (2026-07-20). It does not recover original Java/Kotlin source, and decode fidelity varies by package.

resources.name: Android Studio APK Analyzer
resources.summary: Official Android Studio feature, also available through the apkanalyzer command-line tool, for inspecting APK/AAB contents, DEX structure, manifest, resources, and differences between artifacts. Useful for package inventory and analysis, but it is not a Java/Kotlin source decompiler.

resources.name: Android Debug Bridge (ADB) and Logcat
resources.summary: Official Android SDK Platform-Tools documentation for ADB, which communicates with Android devices and emulators. For live debugging/observation, Android Studio Logcat displays application and system log messages; see the separate official Logcat documentation. These are runtime/debugging tools, not APK decompilers.

resources.name: MobSF (Mobile Security Framework)
resources.summary: Open-source mobile application security-assessment framework. Upstream describes static analysis of mobile app binaries and a dynamic analyzer for Android/iOS testing. It provides automated triage and reports, not a guarantee of complete source recovery or findings.

resources.name: Awesome Reverse Engineering
resources.summary: Community-curated reverse-engineering reference index spanning software, hardware, file-format, and database domains. A discovery reference.

resources.name: GitHub reverse-engineering-tools topic
resources.summary: Dynamic GitHub topic/tag page for repository discovery; listings are community-tagged, change over time, and are not vetted or compatibility evidence. Verify each project at its own upstream.

resources.name: NLInfoSec Reverse Engineering Tools
resources.summary: Community-maintained tool and learning-resource index. Some entries or links may be stale; use it as a discovery lead and verify project status and canonical links upstream.

resources.name: RECESSIM Software Tools
resources.summary: Community wiki index spanning software, firmware, and hardware tools, including niche and potentially legacy entries. It is a broad discovery reference, not a vetted game-modding catalog; check each tool’s domain and status.

resources.name: ZakiRucker Reverse-Engineering
resources.summary: Community-curated learning and tool list; repository activity last checked in 2023, so treat it as a historical discovery reference and verify every entry at its current upstream.

resources.name: Cutter
resources.summary: Open-source graphical reverse-engineering platform powered by Rizin, combining disassembly, decompilation, and analysis views. A general binary-analysis GUI, not a game mod loader; supported formats and target builds must be checked upstream.

resources.name: Rizin
resources.summary: Open-source reverse-engineering framework and command-line toolkit for analyzing binaries. Distinct from Cutter (its GUI) and from the separately catalogued radare2 framework; not a game-specific modding route.

resources.name: IDA Free
resources.summary: Hex-Rays’ free, feature-limited edition of IDA for disassembly and binary analysis; it is separate from the commercial IDA Pro record. Edition limits, supported architectures/formats, and licensing can change; this is not a mod loader.

resources.name: Hopper
resources.summary: Commercial disassembler, decompiler, and debugger for supported desktop binaries. The vendor's free demo disables the debugger backend, prevents saving/exporting, and limits sessions to 30 minutes; these limits were checked 2026-10-07.

resources.name: x64dbg
resources.summary: Open-source Windows user-mode debugger for x86 and x64 programs.

resources.name: WinDbg
resources.summary: Microsoft debugging tools and documentation for Windows user-mode and kernel-mode debugging and dump analysis.

resources.name: GDB
resources.summary: GNU Project debugger for inspecting program execution and crash state on supported targets.

resources.name: LLDB
resources.summary: LLVM debugger for supported platforms and languages, including C-family program debugging. Check platform, target, and symbol support; this is a general debugging tool, not a game modding route.

resources.name: ImHex
resources.summary: Open-source hex editor and binary-format analysis tool with pattern-language support.

resources.name: 010 Editor
resources.summary: Commercial text and binary editor with file templates for structured data inspection. It is an editor, not a game-specific asset pipeline.

resources.name: HxD
resources.summary: Windows hex editor for viewing and editing binary data.

resources.name: Detect It Easy
resources.summary: File-identification utility that reports executable formats and indicators such as likely compilers or packers. Treat results as heuristics and verify upstream definitions.

resources.name: PE-bear
resources.summary: Portable Executable (PE) file-format viewer/editor for Windows executable analysis. Its format scope is PE

resources.name: RetDec
resources.summary: Retargetable machine-code decompiler and binary-analysis framework. Upstream describes the project as being in limited maintenance; confirm current platform, format, and build support before relying on it. Decompiler output is reconstructed analysis, not original source.

resources.name: Snowman
resources.summary: Legacy native-code decompiler project; its repository was archived in 2024. Keep it as a historical reference rather than a current default, and expect limited compatibility with modern binaries.

resources.name: DynamoRIO
resources.summary: Dynamic binary instrumentation framework for runtime program analysis and transformation. This is a specialist development framework, not a mod loader

resources.name: Intel Pin
resources.summary: Intel’s dynamic binary instrumentation framework for building runtime analysis tools. Supported architectures and operating systems are platform-specific; it is not a game-specific modding tool.

resources.name: QEMU
resources.summary: Open-source machine and user-mode emulation platform that can support isolated analysis of supported architectures and systems. Emulation is distinct from decompilation or game modding; firmware, operating-system, and target setup compatibility varies.

resources.name: angr
resources.summary: Python-based binary-analysis framework with program- and symbolic-analysis components. It is a specialist research toolkit rather than a game modding tool; check supported architectures, loaders, and assumptions against the target.

resources.name: BAP (Binary Analysis Platform)
resources.summary: Binary Analysis Platform: libraries and utilities for analyzing programs in machine representation. This is a general analysis framework; verify current development, architecture support, and dependencies before use.

resources.name: Capstone
resources.summary: Multi-architecture disassembly framework/library for embedding instruction decoding in analysis software. It is a component rather than a complete GUI decompiler or game modding workflow.

resources.name: Unicorn
resources.summary: CPU emulation engine/library for supported instruction architectures, often embedded in analysis tooling. It is not a full system emulator or game runtime; confirm architecture and project requirements upstream.

resources.name: radare2
resources.summary: The radare2 reverse-engineering framework itself, with command-line binary-analysis tools. This is distinct from the separately catalogued radare2-mcp connector; it is not a game mod loader.

resources.name: dotPeek
resources.summary: JetBrains.NET assembly browser and decompiler. It can aid managed-code inspection, but reconstructed output is not an original project and does not restore Unity assets, editor state, or source history.

resources.name: dnSpyEx
resources.summary: Community continuation of dnSpy for .NET assembly inspection, decompilation, and debugging. Release/runtime support is project-specific; it is a code-analysis tool, not a game loader.

resources.name: dex2jar
resources.summary: Android DEX-to-Java class/JAR conversion utilities that can support a local analysis pipeline. Conversion may be incomplete and does not recreate original Java/Kotlin source or a buildable project

resources.name: Objection
resources.summary: Frida-powered runtime mobile-app exploration toolkit for Android and iOS.

resources.name: ReVanced Patcher
resources.summary: Library for patching Android applications, including Dalvik bytecode, APK resources, and arbitrary APK files; used by ReVanced Manager and CLI.

resources.name: capa
resources.summary: Mandiant capability-identification tool that applies rules to executable files and reports behaviors for security triage. Specialist malware-analysis reference, not a game-modding utility

resources.name: FLOSS
resources.summary: FLARE Obfuscated String Solver extracts and analyzes strings from supported binaries, especially for malware triage. Specialist analysis reference rather than a general game-code reader

resources.name: YARA
resources.summary: Pattern-matching and classification engine commonly used to identify file and malware characteristics with rules. It is a security-analysis component, not a general game-modding tool

resources.name: CAPE Sandbox
resources.summary: Automated malware-analysis sandbox project for dynamic analysis of samples. Specialist security infrastructure, not a game-modding environment.

resources.name: Volatility 3
resources.summary: Open-source digital memory-forensics framework for analyzing memory images. This is incident-response/forensics tooling, not a game modding or live-process manipulation tool.

resources.name: Wireshark
resources.summary: Network protocol analyzer for inspecting packet captures and troubleshooting systems. Specialist network tooling, not a game modding tool

resources.name: mitmproxy
resources.summary: Interactive HTTP(S) proxy for web-application testing and debugging in controlled environments.

resources.name: Charles Web Debugging Proxy
resources.summary: Cross-platform HTTP(S) web-debugging proxy and monitor for inspecting requests and responses, with HAR import/export. Specialist network tooling.

resources.name: Proxyman
resources.summary: HTTP(S) debugging proxy and traffic analyzer with HAR import/export. Specialist network tooling.

resources.name: Mimic (Python API client generator)
resources.summary: MIT-licensed Python library/CLI for generating API clients from captured app traffic. The README describes mitmproxy, cURL, and HAR inputs, session-data extraction, and authenticated request replay. GitHub showed no tags or releases when checked (2026-10-08); not installed or tested by this index.

resources.name: Burp Suite
resources.summary: PortSwigger web-security testing platform with proxy and application-analysis tools. Specialist web-application security suite, not a general game-modding tool.

resources.name: Netzob
resources.summary: Open-source protocol reverse-engineering framework for characterizing formats and communications from data. Specialist protocol research, not a mod loader

resources.name: Scapy
resources.summary: Python packet-capture, protocol-analysis, and packet-construction toolkit for lab or network troubleshooting. This specialist tool is not a game modding path

resources.name: Binwalk
resources.summary: Firmware-oriented tool for identifying and analyzing embedded data in firmware images. It is not a generic game-asset extractor or game-package tool.

resources.name: FACT (Firmware Analysis and Comparison Tool)
resources.summary: Framework for unpacking, analyzing, and comparing firmware images through a plugin-based workflow. Specialist embedded-device security tooling, not a game-modding utility

resources.name: Saleae Logic
resources.summary: Saleae’s logic-analyzer software for supported Saleae hardware and digital-signal capture/inspection. Hardware and licensing requirements apply; this is an electronics/embedded-systems tool, not game code or asset analysis.

resources.name: sigrok
resources.summary: Open-source signal-analysis software and hardware ecosystem, including logic-analyzer and oscilloscope workflows for supported devices. A specialist electronics reference, not a game-modding tool; check device/driver support upstream.

resources.name: Binary Ninja Cloud
resources.summary: Free browser-hosted Binary Ninja analysis service with more limited features than local clients. The official page lists PE, Mach-O, and ELF support; its cloud feature set is separate from local clients.

resources.name: LLVM MC (llvm-mc)
resources.summary: LLVM machine-code utility for assembling target-specific instructions and disassembling encoded instruction bytes for supported targets. It is a low-level assembler/disassembler component, not a binary-analysis GUI or high-level decompiler; target coverage depends on the LLVM build.

resources.name: CFF Explorer
resources.summary: Windows Portable Executable (PE32/PE32+) inspector/editor included in NTCore Explorer Suite, with support for PE and .NET metadata. NTCore identifies the freeware suite’s current version as III dated 2012-11-18; current package status and compatibility with newer formats are not listed. It is not a general-purpose decompiler.

resources.name: AvaloniaILSpy
resources.summary: Former Avalonia-based cross-platform ILSpy graphical port. The upstream archived it on 2025-07-21 after a long period without maintainers; the current main ILSpy project documents a Windows/Linux/macOS desktop UI, so treat this as a historical reference rather than the current default.

resources.name: de4dot
resources.summary: Legacy.NET deobfuscation utility for some supported obfuscators. The upstream repository was archived on 2020-10-17; compatibility is obfuscator-specific and output is not original source.

resources.name: Bytecode Viewer
resources.summary: Open-source Java/Android bytecode analysis suite for class/JAR and APK/DEX inputs, with multiple decompiler and disassembler backends including CFR, Procyon, FernFlower, and JADX. The upstream labels the inspected 2.13.2 release (2026-01-06) in-development; verify release maturity and dependencies. Decompiled output is approximate and not original source;.

resources.name: CFR
resources.summary: Open-source Java bytecode decompiler for JVM class files and JARs, with support for many modern Java language constructs. Reconstruction can be incomplete or wrong, especially for unusual compiler output or obfuscation; compare with bytecode and other views rather than treating generated Java as source.

resources.name: FernFlower
resources.summary: JetBrains Java bytecode decompiler, also used in IntelliJ-based tools. This is a decompilation engine rather than a complete standalone GUI; reconstructed Java may omit source details or fail to compile.

resources.name: Procyon
resources.summary: Java metaprogramming suite that includes a JVM bytecode decompiler and analysis libraries. The upstream describes the decompiler as experimental; check supported language/compiler features and current maintenance, and treat output as an approximation.

resources.name: WABT (WebAssembly Binary Toolkit)
resources.summary: Official WebAssembly tool suite that includes wasm2wat, wasm-objdump, and wasm-decompile, among other format utilities. wasm-decompile emits readable C-like pseudocode, not the original source language

resources.name: Binaryen
resources.summary: WebAssembly compiler/toolchain infrastructure with utilities including wasm-dis and wasm-opt for parsing, inspecting, optimizing, and emitting modules. It is not a general high-level source decompiler; supported proposals and binary behavior vary by version.

resources.name: de4js
resources.summary: JavaScript deobfuscator/unpacker intended to work locally/offline. The upstream repository was archived on 2021-12-07; supported obfuscators are limited and dated.

resources.name: Chrome DevTools
resources.summary: Google Chrome’s built-in developer tools for inspecting and debugging web pages and applications, including JavaScript and runtime behavior. Source-like views depend on available source maps and build metadata; DevTools is not a general-purpose source decompiler or a game modding API.

resources.name: Firefox Developer Tools
resources.summary: Mozilla’s built-in browser tools for inspecting and debugging web pages and applications, including JavaScript, network activity, and runtime behavior. Debugger views depend on available source maps and build metadata; these tools do not recover original source or provide a generic game modding route.

resources.name: JSDetox
resources.summary: Legacy JavaScript malware-analysis project combining static deobfuscation with an execution engine and HTML DOM emulation. The last upstream code commit located was 2015-01-04; old dependencies and engine behavior limit modern relevance. Historical specialist reference only; use samples in an isolated local lab.

resources.name: Replica Skill (Claude app workflow reference)
resources.summary: MIT-licensed pack of 11 Claude skills for app research, planning, implementation, testing, rebranding, and deployment. The README describes mapping app behavior from public materials and account interactions before planning a separate implementation; its clean-room framing is a project description. GitHub showed one initial commit dated 2026-10-03 and no tags or releases when checked.
